findings.reason: The protected source uses the campaign-forbidden generic local name index for the prefix-array position. The position is a conventional loop coordinate, so i expresses prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + value directly and satisfies the explicit review standard without changing the algorithm.

The inert candidate preserves the Accepted quadratic prefix-sum and middle-separator search byte-for-byte apart from renaming the prefix construction position to i. Its remaining names describe genuine concepts: middle, left, right, prefix, and left_sums. The app-local solve(nums) contract and both complexity bounds are unchanged.

For each legal middle separator, every legal left separator whose first two retained sums match contributes that shared value to left_sums. Every legal right separator then compares its last two retained sums and succeeds only when the same value is realizable on the left. The separator ranges leave all four sections nonempty, and prefix differences exclude i, middle, and right exactly.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 548 and its Python splitArray(nums) interface. The candidate accepts every legal source length from 1 through 2000, returns False naturally when fewer than seven elements cannot form four nonempty sections, and handles negative and zero sums without relying on prefix monotonicity.

The protected app source and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2065347244 are algorithmically identical: both construct an exclusive prefix array, fix the middle separator, collect equal left-half sums, and match equal right-half sums through a set. The candidate changes only one local name and remains inert.

The three exhaustive-miss workloads span array lengths 8 through 64, keep every legal left pair feasible, and force the candidate to complete its quadratic search. The protected source and exact candidate each passed all 12 refreshed correctness cases and all three performance tiers, including the legal 2,000-value boundary. A correct cubic three-separator enumeration passed every benchmark output but failed only scaling with relative growth exponent +1.04 and an 8.60x largest runtime ratio.

The candidate-targeted Approach now exactly describes the i-based prefix construction, exclusive prefix formulas, legal separator ranges, left-sum set, and right-side membership test. Its O(n^2) time and O(n) auxiliary-space claims match the candidate and branch manifest; the malformed middle-variable code span was also corrected.

The modular Reference was reviewed directly in the authenticated Premium statement and bound to its rendered live-content hash. It preserves the exact triplet inequalities, inclusive subarray definition, both source examples and the first explanation, all three constraints, and the legal-but-unsplittable n < 7 domain.

coverage: Both authenticated Premium source examples now appear first and in source order. The incorrect invented second sample was replaced by the exact [1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2] false example.
The all-zero invented sample was relabelled as a trial, and the formerly hidden near-match, mixed-sign miss, and zero-prefix miss are now visible trials.
Contract boundaries cover lengths 1, 6, the minimum splittable length 7, and maximum length 2000, together with values -1000000 and 1000000 and both feasible and infeasible results.

Material semantics cover four nonempty retained sections, removal of all three separator values, zero shared sums, negative and non-monotone prefixes, repeated feasible sums, multi-element sections, and a final section that breaks an otherwise plausible split.

An independent cubic separator oracle verified the eleven non-maximum authored cases and all three benchmark outputs. The maximum case has a direct equal-sum witness at separators (499, 999, 1499), and the protected app, immutable native, and inert candidate sources agreed on 29,523 exhaustive small arrays and 1,000 randomized arrays.
All twelve correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 8-, 32-, and 64-element exhaustive-miss workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
